title: Extracellular and Intracellular pH Measurements in Mice Respiratory Tract In Vivo
author: Faten A Okda
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bu4knyuw
materials: Extracellular pH measurements in live mice
Data were exported via the instrument software and evaluated with GraphPad Prism, v9.0. Statistical comparisons were made with two-way ANOVAs and appropriate posthoc analyses.

Cytosolic pH, microtubule pH, cell membrane pH, and lysozyme pH were measured using pHrodo™ Red AM (Invitrogen, P35372), Paclitaxel, Oregon Green™ 488 (Invitrogen P22310), Oregon Green™ 488 1,2-dihexadecanoyl-sn-glycerol-3-phosphoethanolamine (Oregon Green™ 488 DHPE, O12650), and LysoSensor Blue, respectively.
Cells were washed twice with cold PBS.
Light scatter and DAPI identified cell-sized events.
The dye solution was diluted with 10 mL of LCIS (Cat. no. A14291DJ) and incubated at 37°C for 30 min.
Intracellular pH was quantified by the Intracellular pH Calibration Buffer Kit (Cat. No. P35379).
Calibration and measurement of intracellular pH
The Intracellular pH Calibration Buffer Kit (Cat. no. P35379) was used to clamp the intracellular pH with extracellular buffer.

Four buffers are included in the kit, with pHs of 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, and 7.5. An average of three datapoints was plotted in the graph, and a linear trend line was fitted to obtain the pH standard curve error.

steps.title: Calibrate fiber‑optic pH sensor
steps.instruction: Use the fiber‑optic microsensor (tip diameter 140 µm, tip length 3 mm) and calibrate it with six colorless buffer solutions at pH 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 according to the manufacturer’s instructions to generate a calibration curve.

steps.title: Sterilize microsensor
steps.instruction: Immerse the calibrated sensor in a low‑pH buffer (pH 4) containing Acrylan for in‑house hospital sterilization; verify that the calibration curve remains unchanged.

steps.title: Select anesthetic and measure extracellular pH
steps.instruction: Test ten healthy mice with different anesthetic compounds to identify one that does not interfere with homeostatic pH. Using the calibrated sensor, first measure pH in the nostrils, then carefully introduce the sensor into the nasal cavity to obtain a stable reading without bleeding or irritation, and finally measure soft‑palate pH and tracheal pH with a tracheal catheter. Record salinity and temperature with the same microsensor.

substeps.instruction: Test anesthetic compounds on ten mice and select the non‑interfering anesthetic.
Insert sensor into nasal cavity and record stable pH.
Measure tracheal pH using a tracheal catheter.
Measure salinity and temperature with the microsensor.

steps.title: Prepare and infect mice
steps.instruction: Obtain female DBA2J mice (n = 25, age 4–6 weeks, weight 12–15 g) from Jackson Laboratories, acclimate them at 21–24 °C and 50–65 % humidity, feed standard chow and autoclaved tap water. Divide the mice into three groups of five and intranasally inoculate each mouse with 30 µL of either acid‑stable 2009 pandemic H1N1 virus (WT 750), acid‑destabilized H1N1 virus (HA1‑Y17H 750 or HA1‑Y17H 375K), or PBS.

steps.title: Time‑point sampling and euthanasia
steps.instruction: At 2, 5, 7, and 10 days post‑infection (DPI), randomly select five mice, anesthetize them with isoflurane, and euthanize by cervical dislocation.

steps.title: Collect respiratory tissues
steps.instruction: Immediately place harvested nasal, soft‑palate, and tracheal tissues into sterile microtubes for subsequent intracellular pH analysis.

steps.title: Dissect tissues under sterile conditions
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow hood, pin the euthanized mouse on a dissecting tray, spray with 70 % ethanol, cut off the nasal region with sterile scissors/scalpel, immobilize the head with a suture loop around the front incisors, extract the soft palate, remove skin around the tracheal area, and dissect away fat and salivary glands using sterile instruments.

steps.title: Transfer tissues to collection tubes
steps.instruction: Place each dissected tissue into a 50 mL conical tube containing 30 mL PBS supplemented with 5 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) and antibiotics, keep on ice. Then move the tissue to a 100 mm Petri dish with 10 mL cold buffer and remove connective tissue with sterile forceps and scissors.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion with Pronase
steps.instruction: Wash tissues twice, then incubate them in 10 mL of 0.15 % Pronase solution in a 50 mL tube overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Post‑digestion wash and centrifugation
steps.instruction: Remove tissues from Pronase, wash twice, and centrifuge at 1 400 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: DNAse treatment
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 1 mL DNAse solution (100–200 µL per tissue), incubate 5 min on ice, centrifuge at 1 400 rpm (≈390 ×g) for 5 min at 4 °C, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Negative selection of fibroblasts
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in PBS with FBS, plate onto Falcon Primaria plates, and incubate 5 hr at 37 °C in 95 % air/5 % CO₂ to allow fibroblasts to adhere; non‑adherent cells are retained for further analysis.

steps.title: Prepare intracellular pH reagents
steps.instruction: Gather pH‑sensitive dyes of different wavelengths, Intracellular pH Calibration Buffer Kit (P35379 Live Cell Imaging Solution A14291DJ), and pHrodo™ Green and Red Amine‑Reactive labels (P35369, P36600) and follow the manufacturers’ instructions.

steps.title: Isolate single‑cell suspensions
steps.instruction: From each tissue, collect approximately 2 × 10⁶ cells, centrifuge at 550 × g for 8 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend in 1 mL Sort Buffer to obtain a concentration of 1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Antibody and pH‑marker staining
steps.instruction: Combine cells with the chosen panel of antibodies, pH markers, and isotype controls (three distinct staining sets) and incubate for at least 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Live‑cell gating
steps.instruction: Stain cells with CD4, CD8, and DAPI (note: DAPI is not used in downstream pH assays) to identify live cells for flow cytometry.

steps.title: Flow cytometric sorting
steps.instruction: Sort viable cells using the defined FACS strategy on a BD FACSymphony A5 cytometer (lasers 355, 405, 445, 488, 561, 640 nm, 30 detectors) and collect the sorted population.

steps.title: Intracellular pH staining
steps.instruction: For 200 000–500 000 sorted cells, add 10 µL of the appropriate pH dye to 100 µL PowerLoad™ Concentrate (Fisher Scientific) and incubate according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Final wash and flow analysis
steps.instruction: If needed, wash cells with LCIS, then analyze them on the BD FACSymphony A5 cytometer using the same laser configuration.

steps.title: Quantify intracellular pH
steps.instruction: Determine the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) for each sample relative to three calibration buffers, generate a linear regression, and interpolate cellular pH; higher fluorescence intensity corresponds to lower pH.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Perform interpolation with GraphPad Prism v9, repeat each measurement three times per tissue and animal, and report the results.

steps.title: Collect and filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: After plating, collect the cell suspension, rinse twice with 4 mL PBS containing 10 % FBS, filter through a 40 µm strainer, count cells using trypan blue vital staining, and proceed to staining and sorting as described.
